chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Abu al-Hasan al-Sabati from Ammar ibn Musa, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
"The owner of wealth has more right to his wealth as long as there is a remnant of life in him; he may place it where he wishes."

key_terms.الرُّوح: Life/Soul (here referring to the state of being alive)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on an individual's right to manage their property while alive?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Ruju'* (returning to the will), this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the testator's right to revoke or modify their will is absolute as long as they are alive, reinforcing the principle of *al-Ruju'* in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores that ownership rights are not extinguished by the act of bequeathing but remain fully under the owner's discretion until death, a key distinction from some Sunni schools regarding irrevocability.
